entries.name: Orbital lifetime vs altitude (NASA)
entries.notes: NASA ODPO FAQ: below ~600 km debris normally re-enters within several years; ~800 km often centuries; above ~1,000 km typically 1,000+ years. NASA SST-SOA 2026 deorbit chapter: smallsats ~400 km generally decay in under 5 yr; above ~500 km no 5-yr guarantee, some >25 yr; drag devices usable at <=800 km; solar max vs min can change lifetime by >10 yr; ballistic coeff (Cd 2.2): 6U (6 kg, 0.06 m2) ~45, 100 kg (0.5 m2) ~90. Fig 13.2 plots lifetime vs initial altitude (not extractable as numbers).

entries.name: NASA/IADC 25-year post-mission disposal guideline
entries.notes: NASA-STD-8719.14C: max 25-yr post-mission lifetime in LEO; IADC and FCC (2004) adopted. NASA ODPO 2020: cutting to 5 yr reduces debris population only ~10% over 200 yr (secondary report).

entries.name: FCC 5-year deorbit rule
entries.notes: Adopted Sept 2022 (FCC 22-74): deorbit as soon as practicable, no later than 5 years after mission end; satellites launched after 29 Sep 2024 (Aviation Week via search summary). ESA Zero Debris Approach also moves LEO limit 25->5 yr.
